title: Letter from Reims, 19 June [1589], on the Reims chapter's postulation, in the Nevers-Piles cipher, BnF fr. 20974 pp. 1-3 (DECODE R2276)

documents.shelfmark: BnF fr. 20974 pp. 1-3 (Gallica btv1b9062131g f1-f3; DECODE R2276 images 1-3)
documents.route: Reims -> unknown (a patron who approved the postulation)

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the letter. Tomokiyo (cryptiana guise.htm) reports Norbert Biermann (2021, private communication) found it reads with the Nevers-Piles cipher; no text published.

transcription.source: DECODE R2276 PNGs (3016-3320 px wide), line strips at 1.5-3x; page 3 read rotated 180
transcription.notes: Water damage on the left of p. 2, torn right edge of p. 1 ll. 1-4 and 16-31, stains on p. 3. _check_profile.py --measure --drop-first gives 1632 + 1778 + 563 tokens incl. '...' damage markers; 3920 signs after merging the two-sign codes bb and 3Z (decode.py), the count used by measure.py. Two passes plus relabelling during six reading rounds. Pages in t2.txt and t3.txt.

system.summary: Tomokiyo's Nevers-Piles symbol alphabet: homophones for the common letters, nulls, and code signs for short words, titles and names.
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's partial Nevers-Piles table (from BnF fr. 3612 f. 9, not digitised) and BnF fr. 4715 f. 2 (Cardinal de Guise to Nevers 1586, same cipher, interlinear decipherment; fully aligned here, ~1,050 sign=value pairs, fr4715_values.json).
system.notes: Codes found in this letter beyond Tomokiyo's table: ʒ+Ձ = cardinal, bb = leur, ʒ = le/du, ce-ligature = pour, ꝺ with superscript o = faire, large hooked b = ie, ẋ = vous, ⊞ = parle (from fr. 4715), dotted cursive M = lettre, ⊿ = s. Superscript marks change a sign's value, so diacritics.used is true.

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo, cryptiana guise.htm and unsolved.htm: Biermann (2021, private) found the Nevers-Piles cipher reads it; no reading published

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code, and posed the problem with /goal; cleared the goal at 91.8% and asked for the write-up. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: word-level Viterbi over a 30k-word lexicon with bigrams (wdec.py)
hard-EM re-estimation of per-sign value sets (hardem.py, keyest.py)
subagents for transcription and line-by-line reading against images

solution.what: DECODE R2276 record and three page images fetched with the project cookie.
Tomokiyo guise.htm: fr. 20974 no. 1 'undeciphered'; Biermann 2021 found it reads with the Nevers-Piles cipher (private). Web search: no published text.
Tomokiyo's partial Nevers-Piles table and the orbais/ values from fr. 4715 f. 2.
First pass of all three pages, 93 lines, ~4,000 signs; page 3 read rotated.
Free homophonic anneal under the French 5-gram: collapses to e/s text.
Anneal of unknown labels only with Tomokiyo values fixed: nothing readable.
Polyphonic beam over conflated shapes: words appear (presence, chapitre, chanoines, archidiacre brulart, postulation, lansquenetz, parme, elbeuf).
Second pass: page 1 by hand at 2x, pages 2-3 by two agents; swash-g, open/closed box, new signs split.
Word Viterbi with lexicon and bigrams plus hard-EM on value sets: content identified (Reims chapter postulation, Saint-Remi, Elbeuf ransom, Parma).
Gallica f4 is the letter's verso with the 1556 d'Albany key pasted on: the source of the 1556/Guise attribution, not the letter's key.
Round 1 (agents): date line 'de Reims ... dix neufiesme de iuin', Mayenne, 18,000 lansquenets and 8,000 reiters; many readings were key-conforming non-words.
Tomokiyo's table header (a..z, nulls) read: one value per glyph; conflicts traced to transcription labels.
Extra codes from the readings: ʒ+Ձ = cardinal, d with superscript t = il, ce-ligature = pour, ʒ = du/le, bb = leur; key_v2 to key_v5.
Rounds 2-4 (agents, images, key_v5-v7): p. 1 90%, p. 2 86%, p. 3 88%; codes faire, ie, vous, lettre found.
Targeted round on the '?' words: 107 left; letter strict 88.9%, sense 91.8% (measure.py).
BnF fr. 4715 f. 2 fully aligned with its interlinear (~1,050 pairs): ⊞ = parle, ẋ = vous (never i), swash g = que, ꝺ mostly t in that hand; key_v8.
Escalation recorded: siblings (fr. 4715 f. 2, orbais), clear pages (none), known keys, print (none), key rebuild, retry; remaining gaps blocked by tears, stains, single signs or open codes.

outcome.fraction_read_source: measure.py over reading.txt and t1-t3.txt with key_v7.json: 3598 of 3920 cipher signs aligned to letters of real French words or declared nulls ('?' words and skipped signs count as unread); strict key agreement 3484/3920 = 0.889.

outcome.notes: Read in part. Letter from Reims, 19 June [1589], on the Reims chapter's postulation for the archbishopric (Brulart, Frison), the Elbeuf ransom, Parma. key_v7 is the reading key; key_v8 adds fr. 4715 values.
